ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْأَنْفَالِ قُلِ الْأَنْفَالُ لِلَّهِ وَالرَّسُولِ فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَصْلِحُوا ذَاتَ بَيْنِكُمْ وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ) (١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَنِ الْأَنْفَالِ): the majority pronounce the nūn distinctly (iẓhār), and it is read with the nūn assimilated (idghām) into the lām; this has been mentioned under His saying: عَنِ الْأَهِلَّةِ.
And (ذَاتَ بَيْنِكُمْ): this has been mentioned in Āl ʿImrān under His saying: (بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ).

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا جَعَلَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بُشْرَى وَلِتَطْمَئِنَّ بِهِ قُلُوبُكُمْ وَمَا النَّصْرُ إِلَّا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ) (١٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا جَعَلَهُ اللَّهُ): the hāʾ here is like the hāʾ in Āl ʿImrān.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذْ يُغَشِّيكُمُ النُّعَاسَ أَمَنَةً مِنْهُ وَيُنَزِّلُ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ بِهِ وَيُذْهِبَ عَنْكُمْ رِجْزَ الشَّيْطَانِ وَلِيَرْبِطَ عَلَى قُلُوبِكُمْ وَيُثَبِّتَ بِهِ الْأَقْدَامَ) (١١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ يُغَشِّيكُمُ): «إِذْ» is like [that in] (إِذْ تَسْتَغِيثُونَ); and it may be an adverb (ẓarf) for what is indicated by (عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ).
It is read «يَغْشَاكُمْ», with the light form and an alif, and (النُّعَاسَ) is its fāʿil (agent). It is also read with ḍamma on the yāʾ, kasra on the shīn and a yāʾ after it, with «النُّعَاسَ» in the accusative, i.e. "Allah causes drowsiness to overcome you".
And it is read likewise except with the shīn doubled.
And (أَمَنَةً) is mentioned in Āl ʿImrān.
(مَاءً لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ): the majority read it with the long vowel (madd), and the preposition with its genitive noun is an adjective (ṣifa) to it.
It is read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, with the short form [مَا], in which case it has the meaning of الَّذِي ("that which").
(رِجْزَ الشَّيْطَانِ): the majority read it with zāy, and what is meant by it here is the whispering [of Satan]; it may be called rijz because it is a cause of rijz, which is punishment.
It has been read with sīn; the origin of al-rijs is a filthy thing, so what leads to punishment was made rijs, as a way of deeming it filthy.

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذْ يُوحِي رَبُّكَ إِلَى الْمَلَائِكَةِ أَنِّي مَعَكُمْ فَثَبِّتُوا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا سَأُلْقِي فِي قُلُوبِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا الرُّعْبَ فَاضْرِبُوا فَوْقَ الْأَعْنَاقِ وَاضْرِبُوا مِنْهُمْ كُلَّ بَنَانٍ) (١٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَوْقَ الْأَعْنَاقِ): it is the adverb (ẓarf) of ضَرَبُوا «[Translator's note: so in the text, for اضْرِبُوا]»; and what is above the neck is the head.
It is also said: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). And it is said: فَوْقَ is redundant (zāʾida). (مِنْهُمْ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «كُلَّ بَنَانٍ», i.e. "every fingertip, being of them".
It is weak for it to be a ḥāl from بَنَانٍ, since that would involve putting the ḥāl of the muḍāf ilayhi before the muḍāf.

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ شَاقُّوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَمَنْ يُشَاقِقِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ) (١٣).
(ذَلِكَ): i.e. "the matter is that". It is also said: ذَلِكَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject).
And (بِأَنَّهُمْ) is the khabar (predicate), i.e. "that is deserved because of their opposition".
(وَمَنْ يُشَاقِقِ اللَّهَ): it was not assimilated only because the second qāf is vowelless in origin, and its vowel here is due to the meeting of two vowelless letters, so it is not taken into account.

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكُمْ فَذُوقُوهُ وَأَنَّ لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابَ النَّارِ) (١٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ذَلِكُمْ فَذُوقُوهُ): i.e. "the matter is that", or "that is taking place", or "is deserved". It may be in the position of the accusative, i.e. "taste that", the verb after it being made an explanation (mufassir) of it; but it is better for the implied wording to be: "undergo that, and taste it" (بَاشِرُوا ذَلِكُمْ فَذُقُوهُ), so that the fāʾ is a conjunction. (وَأَنَّ لِلْكَافِرِينَ): i.e. "and the matter is that for the disbelievers…".

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا لَقِيتُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا زَحْفًا فَلَا تُوَلُّوهُمُ الْأَدْبَارَ) (١٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (زَحْفًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).
It is also said: it is the maṣdar of an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "advancing (تَزْحَفُونَ) an advance". And (الْأَدْبَارَ) is the second object of تُوَلُّوهُمْ.

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَنْ يُوَلِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ دُبُرَهُ إِلَّا مُتَحَرِّفًا لِقِتَالٍ أَوْ مُتَحَيِّزًا إِلَى فِئَةٍ فَقَدْ بَاءَ بِغَضَبٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَمَأْوَاهُ جَهَنَّمُ وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ) (١٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مُتَحَرِّفًا), (أَوْ مُتَحَيِّزًا): two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the agent pronoun in يُوَلِّهِمْ.

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكُمْ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ مُوهِنُ كَيْدِ الْكَافِرِينَ) (١٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ذَلِكُمْ): i.e. "the matter is that", «and» the matter is «that Allah is the weakener (مُوهِنُ)» — [read] with the hāʾ doubled and undoubled, and with the genitive construct and with tanwīn; this is clear.

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنْ تَسْتَفْتِحُوا فَقَدْ جَاءَكُمُ الْفَتْحُ وَإِنْ تَنْتَهُوا فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ وَإِنْ تَعُودُوا نَعُدْ وَلَنْ تُغْنِيَ عَنْكُمْ فِئَتُكُمْ شَيْئًا وَلَوْ كَثُرَتْ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) (١٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): it is read with kasra [إِنَّ] as a new beginning (istiʾnāf), and with fatḥa on the implied wording: "and the matter is that Allah is with the believers".

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَإِذَا تُلِيَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتُهُ زَادَتْهُمْ إِيمَانًا وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ) (٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَجِلَتْ): its imperfect is تَوْجَلُ, with fatḥa on the tāʾ and sukūn on the wāw, and this is the good dialect. Some of them change the wāw into an alif for lightness; and some of them change it into a yāʾ after giving kasra to the tāʾ — this is according to the dialect of those who give kasra to the imperfect prefix, and the wāw changed into yāʾ because it is vowelless and what precedes it has kasra. And some of them give fatḥa to the tāʾ together with a vowelless yāʾ, so that a third dialect is compounded out of the two dialects: the first letter is given fatḥa according to the widespread dialect, and the wāw is changed into yāʾ according to the other. (وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ): the clause may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object pronoun in زَادَتْهُمْ, and it may be resumptive (mustaʾnaf).

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ شَرَ الدَّوَابِّ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الصُّمُّ الْبُكْمُ الَّذِينَ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ) (٢٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنَّ شَرَّ الدَّوَابِّ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الصُّمُّ): الصُّمّ was put in the plural, while it is the khabar (predicate) of «شَرَّ», only because شَرّ here is meant to denote multiplicity, so the khabar was put in the plural according to the meaning. Had He said الْأَصَمَّ, the singular would have been according to the wording, while the meaning is plural.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ حَقًّا لَهُمْ دَرَجَاتٌ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ وَرِزْقٌ كَرِيمٌ) (٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حَقًّا): the like of it has been mentioned in al-Nisāʾ.
And (عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ): an adverb (ẓarf), and what governs it is [the notion of] settledness (al-istiqrār). It is also possible that what governs it is دَرَجَاتٍ, because what is meant by it is the rewards.

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَمَا أَخْرَجَكَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَيْتِكَ بِالْحَقِّ وَإِنَّ فَرِيقًا مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ لَكَارِهُونَ) (٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَمَا أَخْرَجَكَ): there are several views on the position of the kāf. The first: it is an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), and then there are several views on that maṣdar; [one is that] its implied form is: "[the spoils] are established as belonging to Allah, an establishment like [the way] He brought you out" (ثَابِتَةٌ لِلَّهِ ثُبُوتًا كَمَا أَخْرَجَكَ). The second: "and set right what is between you, a setting-right like [the way] He brought you out" (وَأَصْلَحُوا ذَاتَ بَيْنِكُمْ إِصْلَاحًا كَمَا أَخْرَجَكَ); in this there is a return from addressing the plural to addressing the singular. The third: its implied form is: "and obey Allah, an obedience like [the way] He brought you out" (وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ طَاعَةً كَمَا أَخْرَجَكَ), the meaning being "a realised obedience". The fourth: its implied form is: "they rely, a reliance like [the way] He brought you out" (يَتَوَكَّلُونَ تَوَكُّلًا كَمَا أَخْرَجَكَ). The fifth: it is an adjective of حَقًّا, its implied form being: "those are the believers truly, like what He brought you out" (أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ حَقًّا؛ مِثْلُ مَا أَخْرَجَكَ). The sixth: its implied form is: "they dispute with you, a disputing like [the way] He brought you out" (يُجَادِلُونَكَ جِدَالًا كَمَا أَخْرَجَكَ). The seventh: its implied form is: "while they were averse, an aversion like [the way] He brought you out" (وَهُمْ كَارِهُونَ كَرَاهِيَةً كَمَا أَخْرَجَكَ), i.e. like their aversion, or your aversion, to your being brought out.
Some have held that the kāf is in the meaning of the wāw of the oath, but this is far-fetched.
And «مَا» is maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar), and «بِالْحَقِّ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); its parallels have been mentioned. (وَإِنَّ فَرِيقًا): the wāw here is the wāw of the ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ يَعِدُكُمُ اللَّهُ إِحْدَى الطَّائِفَتَيْنِ أَنَّهَا لَكُمْ وَتَوَدُّونَ أَنَّ غَيْرَ ذَاتِ الشَّوْكَةِ تَكُونُ لَكُمْ وَيُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُحِقَّ الْحَقَّ بِكَلِمَاتِهِ وَيَقْطَعَ دَابِرَ الْكَافِرِينَ) (٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِذْ يَعِدُكُمُ): إِذْ is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "and remember". The majority read it with ḍamma on the dāl, and some give it sukūn for lightness, because of the succession of vowels. And (إِحْدَى) is the second object.
And (أَنَّهَا لَكُمْ) is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from إِحْدَى, a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl); the implied wording is: "and when Allah promised you possession of one of the two parties" (وَإِذْ يَعِدُكُمُ اللَّهُ مَلَكَةَ إِحْدَى الطَّائِفَتَيْنِ).

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذْ تَسْتَغِيثُونَ رَبَّكُمْ فَاسْتَجَابَ لَكُمْ أَنِّي مُمِدُّكُمْ بِأَلْفٍ مِنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ مُرْدِفِينَ) (٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ تَسْتَغِيثُونَ): it may be a badal (substitute) from the first «إِذْ», or the implied wording may be "remember"; and it may be an adverb (ẓarf) for تَوَدُّونَ.
(بِأَلْفٍ): the majority read the word أَلْف in the singular.
It is also read «بِآلُفٍ», on the pattern afʿul, like أَفْلُسٍ; and this is the meaning of His saying: (بِخَمْسَةِ آلَافٍ).
(مُرْدِفِينَ): it is read with ḍamma on the mīm, kasra on the dāl and sukūn on the rāʾ; its verb is «أَرْدَفَ», and the object is omitted, i.e. "followed by others like them" (مُرْدِفِينَ أَمْثَالَهُمْ).
It is also read with fatḥa on the dāl, as a passive (mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu), i.e. "they were followed up with others like them".
And it is possible that al-murdafūn are those who came after the first ones, i.e. they were made to follow behind the first ones. It is also read with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the dāl and doubling it; on this reading there are three possibilities for the rāʾ:
Fatḥa: its origin is مُرْتَدِفِينَ; the vowel of the tāʾ was transferred to the rāʾ, and [the tāʾ] was replaced by a dāl so that it could be assimilated into the dāl. Changing the tāʾ was preferable because it is voiceless (mahmūsa) while the dāl is voiced (majhūra), and changing the weak into the strong is preferable. The second: kasra on the rāʾ, by making it follow (itbāʿ) the kasra of the dāl, or according to the basic rule for the meeting of two vowelless letters. The third: ḍamma, following the ḍamma of the mīm.
It is also read with kasra on the mīm and the rāʾ, by making the mīm follow the rāʾ.
It is also said: whoever reads with fatḥa on the rāʾ and doubling of the dāl, it is from رَدَّفَ, with the middle radical doubled for intensiveness; or else the doubling is a substitute for the hamza [of the afʿala form], as in أَفْرَجْتُهُ and فَرَّجْتُهُ.

ukberi-tibyan:25-25.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاتَّقُوا فِتْنَةً لَا تُصِيبَنَّ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْكُمْ خَاصَّةً وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا تُصِيبَنَّ): there are three views on it. The first: it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf), and it is the response to an omitted oath, i.e. "By Allah, it will not strike those who did wrong exclusively; rather it will be general". The second: it is a prohibition, and the statement is taken according to the meaning, as you say: لَا أَرَيَنَّكَ هَاهُنَا ("let me not see you here"), i.e. "do not be here, for whoever is here, I will see him". Likewise the meaning here, since the meaning is: "do not enter into the fitna (trial), for whoever enters into it, a general punishment will descend upon him". The third: it is the response to the command, and it was emphasised with the nūn for intensity; but this is weak, because the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is uncertain, so emphasis does not suit it.
It was read, among the irregular (shādhdh) readings: (لَتُصِيبَنَّ), without an alif. Ibn Jinnī said: the most likely thing is that the alif has been dropped, just as it was dropped in أَمَ وَاللَّهِ.
It is also said, regarding the reading of the majority, that the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of فِتْنَةً, and the nūn entered upon a negated [verb] outside an oath, as an irregularity (shudhūdh).

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاذْكُرُوا إِذْ أَنْتُمْ قَلِيلٌ مُسْتَضْعَفُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ تَخَافُونَ أَنْ يَتَخَطَّفَكُمُ النَّاسُ فَآوَاكُمْ وَأَيَّدَكُمْ بِنَصْرِهِ وَرَزَقَكُمْ مِنَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ) (٢٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تَخَافُونَ): it may be in the position of the nominative as an adjective (ṣifa), like what precedes it, i.e. "fearing" (خَائِفُونَ); and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «مُسْتَضْعَفُونَ».

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَخُونُوا اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ وَتَخُونُوا أَمَانَاتِكُمْ وَأَنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ) (٢٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَتَخُونُوا أَمَانَاتِكُمْ): it may be jussive (majzūm), conjoined to the first verb, or accusative as a response with the wāw.

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ يَمْكُرُ بِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِيُثْبِتُوكَ أَوْ يَقْتُلُوكَ أَوْ يُخْرِجُوكَ وَيَمْكُرُونَ وَيَمْكُرُ اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الْمَاكِرِينَ) (٣٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِذْ يَمْكُرُ): it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to: (وَاذْكُرُوا إِذْ أَنْتُمْ).

ukberi-tibyan:32-32.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ قَالُوا اللَّهُمَّ إِنْ كَانَ هَذَا هُوَ الْحَقَّ مِنْ عِنْدِكَ فَأَمْطِرْ عَلَيْنَا حِجَارَةً مِنَ السَّمَاءِ أَوِ ائْتِنَا بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ) (٣٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هُوَ الْحَقَّ): the well-known reading is with the accusative, and «هُوَ» here is a separating pronoun (faṣl).
It is also read with the nominative, on the basis that «هُوَ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and الْحَقُّ its khabar (predicate), the clause being the khabar of كَانَ.
And (مِنْ عِنْدِكَ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the meaning of الْحَقّ, i.e. "that which is established from You".
(مِنَ السَّمَاءِ): it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to أَمْطِرْ, and it may be an adjective (ṣifa) of حِجَارَةً.

ukberi-tibyan:34-34.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا لَهُمْ أَلَّا يُعَذِّبَهُمُ اللَّهُ وَهُمْ يَصُدُّونَ عَنِ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ وَمَا كَانُوا أَوْلِيَاءَهُ إِنْ أَوْلِيَاؤُهُ إِلَّا الْمُتَّقُونَ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ) (٣٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَلَّا يُعَذِّبَهُمُ): i.e. "in that He should not punish them", so it is in the position of the accusative or the genitive, according to the disagreement [on the omitted preposition]. It is also said: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial); but this is far-fetched, because «أَنْ» restricts the verb to the future.

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا كَانَ صَلَاتُهُمْ عِنْدَ الْبَيْتِ إِلَّا مُكَاءً وَتَصْدِيَةً فَذُوقُوا الْعَذَابَ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ) (٣٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا كَانَ صَلَاتُهُمْ): the majority read الصَّلَاة in the nominative and الْمُكَاء in the accusative, and this is clear.
Al-Aʿmash read it the other way round, and this is weak. Its justification is that الْمُكَاء and الصَّلَاة are both maṣdars (verbal nouns), and the maṣdar is a genus, and the definite of a genus is close to its indefinite, and its indefinite is close to its definite. Do you not see that there is no difference between "I went out and lo, the lion" (خَرَجْتُ فَإِذَا الْأَسَدُ) or "and lo, a lion" (فَإِذَا أَسَدٌ)? This is strengthened by the fact that negation and affirmation have entered the statement, and in that, what is not good in pure affirmation may be good. Do you not see that it is not good to say كَانَ رَجُلٌ خَيْرًا مِنْكَ ("a man was better than you"), while it is good to say مَا كَانَ رَجُلٌ إِلَّا خَيْرًا مِنْكَ ("no man was but better than you")?
The hamza of الْمُكَاء is a replacement for a wāw, because of their saying مَكَا يَمْكُو.
The origin of التَّصْدِيَة is تَصْدِدَةٌ, because it is from al-ṣadd (turning away); the last dāl was replaced by a yāʾ because of the heaviness of the doubling. It is also said: [the yāʾ] is original, and it is from al-ṣadā, which is the sound [echo].

ukberi-tibyan:37-37.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِيَمِيزَ اللَّهُ الْخَبِيثَ مِنَ الطَّيِّبِ وَيَجْعَلَ الْخَبِيثَ بَعْضَهُ عَلَى بَعْضٍ فَيَرْكُمَهُ جَمِيعًا فَيَجْعَلَهُ فِي جَهَنَّمَ أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْخَاسِرُونَ) (٣٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِيَمِيزَ): it is read with doubling and without; this has been mentioned in Āl ʿImrān.
And (بَعْضَهُ) is a badal (substitute) from الْخَبِيث, a badal of part (badal al-baʿḍ), i.e. "some of the foul upon some".
And (يَجْعَلُ) here is transitive to one object by itself and to the second by means of a preposition.
It is also said: the preposition and its genitive noun are a ḥāl (circumstantial), its implied form being: "and He makes some of the foul high upon some".

ukberi-tibyan:40-40.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ مَوْلَاكُمْ نِعْمَ الْمَوْلَى وَنِعْمَ النَّصِيرُ) (٤٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نِعْمَ الْمَوْلَى): the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted, i.e. "an excellent Protector is Allah, glory be to Him".

ukberi-tibyan:41-41.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا غَنِمْتُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَأَنَّ لِلَّهِ خُمُسَهُ وَلِلرَّسُولِ وَلِذِي الْقُرْبَى وَالْيَتَامَى وَالْمَسَاكِينِ وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ آمَنْتُمْ بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَى عَبْدِنَا يَوْمَ الْفُرْقَانِ يَوْمَ الْتَقَى الْجَمْعَانِ وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) (٤٦) «[Translator's note: so numbered in the text; this is verse 41]».
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنَّمَا غَنِمْتُمْ): «مَا» is in the meaning of الَّذِي ("that which"), and the returning pronoun (al-ʿāʾid) is omitted.
And (مِنْ شَيْءٍ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted returning pronoun, its implied form being: "what you have taken as spoil, little and much".
(فَأَنَّ لِلَّهِ): it is read with fatḥa on the hamza, and there are two views on the fāʾ:
The first: it has entered the khabar (predicate) of الَّذِي because of the sense of requital (al-mujāzāh) in الَّذِي; and «أَنَّ» together with what it governs is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "then the ruling is that to Allah belongs a fifth of it". The second: the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and (أَنَّ) is a badal (substitute) from the first [أَنَّ]. It is also said: «مَا» is maṣdariyya, and the maṣdar is in the meaning of the passive participle, i.e. "and know that your spoil", i.e. "what you have taken as spoil".
It is also read with kasra on the hamza in the second «إِنَّ», on the basis that «إِنَّ» and what it governs are a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the khabar of the first. And الْخُمُس with ḍamma on the mīm and with sukūn are two dialectal forms, and both have been read.
(يَوْمَ الْفُرْقَانِ): an adverb (ẓarf) for أَنْزَلْنَا or for آمَنْتُمْ.
(يَوْمَ الْتَقَى): a badal from the first «يَوْمَ»; and it may be an adverb for الْفُرْقَان, because it is a maṣdar in the meaning of "separating" (al-tafrīq).

ukberi-tibyan:42-42.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذْ أَنْتُمْ بِالْعُدْوَةِ الدُّنْيَا وَهُمْ بِالْعُدْوَةِ الْقُصْوَى وَالرَّكْبُ أَسْفَلَ مِنْكُمْ وَلَوْ تَوَاعَدْتُمْ لَاخْتَلَفْتُمْ فِي الْمِيعَادِ وَلَكِنْ لِيَقْضِيَ اللَّهُ أَمْرًا كَانَ مَفْعُولًا لِيَهْلِكَ مَنْ هَلَكَ عَنْ بَيِّنَةٍ وَيَحْيَا مَنْ حَيَّ عَنْ بَيِّنَةٍ وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَسَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ) (٤٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ أَنْتُمْ): «إِذْ» is also a badal (substitute) from «يَوْمَ»; and the implied wording may be: "remember when you were…".
It may also be an adverb (ẓarf) for قَدِيرٌ. And الْعُدْوَة with ḍamma and with kasra are two dialectal forms, and both have been read.
(الْقُصْوَى): with wāw; it departs [from the usual rule] by keeping the original, its origin being from wāw. The rule of usage is that it should be الْقُصْيَا «[Translator's note: the text vocalises it الْقِصْيَا]», because it is an adjective like الدُّنْيَا and الْعُلْيَا, and when fuʿlā is an adjective its wāw is changed into yāʾ, to distinguish between the noun and the adjective.
(وَالرَّكْبُ): a plural of رَاكِبٍ in meaning, but not a plural in form; for this reason you say in the diminutive رُكَيْبٌ, just as you say فُرَيْخٌ.
And (أَسْفَلَ مِنْكُمْ) is an adverb, i.e. "and the caravan was in a place lower than you", i.e. "lower down"; and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the adverbial phrase before it.
It may also be in the position of the genitive, conjoined to أَنْتُمْ, i.e. "and when (وَإِذَا) the caravan was lower than you".
(لِيَقْضِيَ اللَّهُ): i.e. "He did that in order to accomplish…".
(لِيَهْلِكَ): it may be a badal from لِيَقْضِيَ with repetition of the particle, and it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَقْضِيَ» or to «مَفْعُولًا».
(مَنْ هَلَكَ): the past here is in the meaning of the future. The meaning may also be: "so that those of them who perished in this world by being killed might perish by the punishment of the Hereafter".
(مَنْ حَيَّ): it is read with the yāʾ doubled, and this is the original rule, because the two letters are identical and voweled, so it is like شَدَّ and مَدَّ. Of this kind is the saying of ʿUbayd:
عَيُّوا بِأَمْرِهِمُ كَمَا عَيَّتْ بِبَيْضَتِهَا الْحَمَامَهْ
("They were at a loss over their affair, as the dove was at a loss over its egg")
It is also read with the two kept distinct (iẓhār), and there are two views on this. The first: the past was modelled on the imperfect, which is يَحْيَا; just as there is no assimilation in the imperfect, there is none in the past. شَدَّ and مَدَّ are not like this, for assimilation takes place in both [tenses].
The second view: the vowels of the two letters differ — the first has kasra and the second fatḥa — and a difference of the two vowels is like a difference of the two letters. For this reason they permitted, by free choice, لَحِحَتْ عَيْنُهُ ("his eye became sore") and ضَبِبَ الْبَلَدُ, said when its lizards (ḍabb) are many. This is strengthened by the fact that the second vowel is incidental, so it is as if the second yāʾ were vowelless; and had it been made vowelless, assimilation would not be necessary; and likewise when it is in the virtual state of being vowelless. Both yāʾs are original, and the second is not a replacement for a wāw. As for الْحَيَوَان, the wāw in it is a replacement for the yāʾ; and as for الْحِوَاء, it is not from the root of الْحَيَّة (the snake) but from حَوَى يَحْوِي, said when one gathers.
And (عَنْ بَيِّنَةٍ) in both places is attached to the first verb.

ukberi-tibyan:43-43.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذْ يُرِيكَهُمُ اللَّهُ فِي مَنَامِكَ قَلِيلًا وَلَوْ أَرَاكَهُمْ كَثِيرًا لَفَشِلْتُمْ وَلَتَنَازَعْتُمْ فِي الْأَمْرِ وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ سَلَّمَ إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ) (٤٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ يُرِيكَهُمُ): i.e. "remember"; and it may be an adverb (ẓarf) for (عَلِيمٌ).

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَلَا تَنَازَعُوا فَتَفْشَلُوا وَتَذْهَبَ رِيحُكُمْ وَاصْبِرُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ) (٤٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَتَفْشَلُوا): in the position of the accusative as the response to the prohibition; and likewise «وَتَذْهَبَ رِيحُكُمْ».
It is also possible for فَتَفْشَلُوا to be jussive, conjoined to the prohibition; and for this reason it has been read «وَيَذْهَبْ رِيحُكُمْ».

ukberi-tibyan:47-47.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا مِنْ دِيَارِهِمْ بَطَرًا وَرِئَاءَ النَّاسِ وَيَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ مُحِيطٌ) (٤٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَطَرًا وَرِئَاءَ النَّاسِ): a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(وَيَصُدُّونَ): conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the meaning of the maṣdar.

ukberi-tibyan:48-48.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ زَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ أَعْمَالَهُمْ وَقَالَ لَا غَالِبَ لَكُمُ الْيَوْمَ مِنَ النَّاسِ وَإِنِّي جَارٌ لَكُمْ فَلَمَّا تَرَاءَتِ الْفِئَتَانِ نَكَصَ عَلَى عَقِبَيْهِ وَقَالَ إِنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِنْكُمْ إِنِّي أَرَى مَا لَا تَرَوْنَ إِنِّي أَخَافُ اللَّهَ وَاللَّهُ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ) (٤٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا غَالِبَ لَكُمُ الْيَوْمَ): «غَالِبَ» here is indeclinable (mabnī), and لَكُمْ is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «لَا», and الْيَوْمَ is governed by the khabar.
And (مِنَ النَّاسِ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in لَكُمْ. It is not permissible for «الْيَوْمَ» to be made accusative by «غَالِبَ», nor for مِنَ النَّاسِ to be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «غَالِبَ», because when the noun of «لَا» governs what comes after it, it may not be indeclinable.
The alif in «جَارٌ» is a replacement for a wāw, because you say جَاوَرْتُهُ.
And (عَلَى عَقِبَيْهِ) is a ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:49-49.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذْ يَقُولُ الْمُنَافِقُونَ وَالَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ غَرَّ هَؤُلَاءِ دِينُهُمْ وَمَنْ يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ) (٤٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ يَقُولُ الْمُنَافِقُونَ): i.e. "remember"; and it may be an adverb (ẓarf) for زَيَّنَ, or for any of the verbs mentioned in the verse with which the meaning holds good.

ukberi-tibyan:50-50.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْ تَرَى إِذْ يَتَوَفَّى الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا الْمَلَائِكَةُ يَضْرِبُونَ وُجُوهَهُمْ وَأَدْبَارَهُمْ وَذُوقُوا عَذَابَ الْحَرِيقِ) (٥٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَتَوَفَّى): it is read with yāʾ, and there are two views on the fāʿil (agent). The first: it is «الْمَلَائِكَةُ», and [the verb] was not made feminine because of the separation between them, and because the femininity of الْمَلَائِكَة is not real. On this view «يَضْرِبُونَ وُجُوهَهُمْ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْمَلَائِكَة, or a ḥāl from الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا, because it contains a pronoun referring to each of them. The second: the agent is a latent pronoun, i.e. "when Allah takes [them] in death"; on this view الْمَلَائِكَة is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and يَضْرِبُونَ the khabar (predicate), and the clause is a ḥāl; it did not need the wāw because of the pronoun, i.e. "He takes them in death while the angels strike their faces". It is also read with tāʾ, and the agent is الْمَلَائِكَة.

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ كَفَرُوا بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ فَأَخَذَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ) (٥٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَدَأْبِ): what makes the i'rab of this place sound has been mentioned in Āl ʿImrān.

ukberi-tibyan:53-53.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ لَمْ يَكُ مُغَيِّرًا نِعْمَةً أَنْعَمَهَا عَلَى قَوْمٍ حَتَّى يُغَيِّرُوا مَا بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ) (٥٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ): it is read with fatḥa on the hamza, its implied form being: "that is because Allah would not change…, and because Allah is All-Hearing"; and it is read with kasra on it, as a new beginning (istiʾnāf).

ukberi-tibyan:56-56.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ عَاهَدْتَ مِنْهُمْ ثُمَّ يَنْقُضُونَ عَهْدَهُمْ فِي كُلِّ مَرَّةٍ وَهُمْ لَا يَتَّقُونَ) (٥٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ عَاهَدْتَ): it may be a badal (substitute) from the first الَّذِينَ, and it may be the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are those who…".
It may also be accusative by an implied أَعْنِي ("I mean"). And مِنْهُمْ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted returning pronoun.

ukberi-tibyan:57-57.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِمَّا تَثْقَفَنَّهُمْ فِي الْحَرْبِ فَشَرِّدْ بِهِمْ مَنْ خَلْفَهُمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ) (٥٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَإِمَّا تَثْقَفَنَّهُمْ): when the conditional «إِنْ» is emphasised with «مَا», the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) is emphasised with the nūn, so that the meaning is consistent.
(فَشَرِّدْ بِهِمْ): the majority read it with dāl, and this is the original.
Al-Aʿmash read it with dhāl, and it is a replacement for the dāl, just as they said خَرَادِيلُ and خَرَاذِيلُ «[Translator's note: the text has خَزَاذِيلُ]». It is also said: it is transposed (maqlūb) from شَذَّرَ, meaning "to scatter", and from it is their saying: تَفَرَّقُوا شَذَرَ مَذَرَ ("they scattered in all directions"). And it may be from شَذَرَ فِي مَقَالِهِ, said when one speaks excessively. All of this is forced and far-fetched.

ukberi-tibyan:58-58.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِمَّا تَخَافَنَّ مِنْ قَوْمٍ خِيَانَةً فَانْبِذْ إِلَيْهِمْ عَلَى سَوَاءٍ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْخَائِنِينَ) (٥٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَانْبِذْ إِلَيْهِمْ): i.e. "their covenant"; the object has been omitted.
And (عَلَى سَوَاءٍ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:59-59.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا سَبَقُوا إِنَّهُمْ لَا يُعْجِزُونَ) (٥٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ): it is read with tāʾ, as an address to the Prophet ﷺ, and the second object is «سَبَقُوا».
It is also read with yāʾ, and there are two views on the fāʿil (agent). The first: it is latent (muḍmar), i.e. "let those behind them not think", or "let no one think"; on this view the i'rab is like that of the first reading.
The second: the agent is الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا, and the second object is «سَبَقُوا», while the first is omitted, i.e. "themselves". It is also said that the implied wording is أَنْ سَبَقُوا, with أَنْ here being maṣdariyya, lightened from the heavy form [أَنَّ]; this is reported from al-Farrāʾ, but it is far-fetched, because maṣdariyya «أَنْ» is a relative (mawṣūl), and omitting the relative is weak by analogy and irregular in usage.
(إِنَّهُمْ لَا يُعْجِزُونَ): i.e. "let them not think that, because of this." The second: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to تَحْسَبُ, either as an object or as a badal (substitute) from سَبَقُوا; and on both of these views لَا is redundant (zāʾida). This is weak for two reasons. The first: the redundancy of لَا. The second: when the object of حَسِبْتُ is a clause and is the second object, إِنَّ in it has kasra, because it is the place of a mubtadaʾ and khabar.
«[Translator's note: the first view on this phrase is not labelled as such in the text; it is the explanation that precedes "The second".]»

ukberi-tibyan:60-60.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَعِدُّوا لَهُمْ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ مِنْ قُوَّةٍ وَمِنْ رِبَاطِ الْخَيْلِ تُرْهِبُونَ بِهِ عَدُوَّ اللَّهِ وَعَدُوَّكُمْ وَآخَرِينَ مِنْ دُونِهِمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَهُمُ اللَّهُ يَعْلَمُهُمْ وَمَا تُنْفِقُوا مِنْ شَيْءٍ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ يُوَفَّ إِلَيْكُمْ وَأَنْتُمْ لَا تُظْلَمُونَ) (٦٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ قُوَّةٍ): it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مَا» or from the omitted returning pronoun in «اسْتَطَعْتُمْ». (تُرْهِبُونَ بِهِ): in the position of a ḥāl from the agent in اعْدِلُوا «[Translator's note: so in the text, for أَعِدُّوا]», or from the object, because the clause contains two pronouns referring to them.

ukberi-tibyan:61-61.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنْ جَنَحُوا لِلسَّلْمِ فَاجْنَحْ لَهَا وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ) (٦١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِلسَّلْمِ): the lām may be in the meaning of إِلَى ("to"), because جَنَحَ means "to incline". It may also be [a lām] that itself makes the verb transitive, and it may be in the meaning of "for the sake of" (مِنْ أَجْلِ). And «السَّلْم» with kasra on the sīn and with fatḥa are two dialectal forms, and both have been read. It is feminine, and for this reason He said: «فَاجْنَحْ لَهَا».

ukberi-tibyan:64-64.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ حَسْبُكَ اللَّهُ وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَكَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) (٦٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حَسْبُكَ اللَّهُ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). Some said: حَسْبُكَ is a mubtadaʾ and اللَّهُ is its fāʿil (agent), i.e. "Allah suffices you".
(وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَكَ): there are three views on «مَنْ». The first: genitive, conjoined to the kāf in حَسْبُكَ; but this is not permissible according to the Basrans, because conjoining to a genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition is not permissible. The second: its position is accusative by an omitted verb indicated by the context, its implied form being: "and [Allah] suffices those who follow you".
The third: its position is nominative, in three ways. The first: it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the name of Allah, so it is another khabar, as when you say الْقَائِمَانِ زَيْدٌ وَعَمْرٌو ("the two standing are Zayd and ʿAmr"); حَسْبُكَ was not put in the dual because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun).
Some said: this is weak, because the wāw is for combining, and it is not good here, just as it is not good in their saying مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ وَشِئْتَ ("what Allah willed and you willed"); ثُمَّ ("then") would be more appropriate there. The second: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "and those who follow you suffice you".
«[Translator's note: the text announces three ways for the nominative but gives only two.]»

ukberi-tibyan:65-65.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ حَرِّضِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَى الْقِتَالِ إِنْ يَكُنْ مِنْكُمْ عِشْرُونَ صَابِرُونَ يَغْلِبُوا مِائَتَيْنِ وَإِنْ يَكُنْ مِنْكُمْ مِائَةٌ يَغْلِبُوا أَلْفًا مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لَا يَفْقَهُونَ) (٦٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنْ يَكُنْ): it may be the complete (tāmma) [kāna], so that the fāʿil (agent) is «عِشْرُونَ», and (مِنْكُمْ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it, or is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يَكُنْ.
It may also be the incomplete (nāqiṣa) [kāna], so that عِشْرُونَ is its noun and «مِنْكُمْ» the khabar (predicate).

ukberi-tibyan:67-67.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَا كَانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ أَسْرَى حَتَّى يُثْخِنَ فِي الْأَرْضِ تُرِيدُونَ عَرَضَ الدُّنْيَا وَاللَّهُ يُرِيدُ الْآخِرَةَ وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ) (٦٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَسْرَى): there are readings of it which have been mentioned in al-Baqara.
(وَاللَّهُ يُرِيدُ الْآخِرَةَ): the majority read الْآخِرَة in the accusative, as is obvious. It was read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, in the genitive, its implied form being: "and Allah wants the goods of the Hereafter"; the muḍāf was omitted and its governing effect remained, as one of them said:
أَكُلَّ امْرِئٍ تَحْسَبِينَ امْرَأً ... وَنَارٍ تَوَقَّدُ بِاللَّيْلِ نَارًا
("Do you reckon every man a [true] man, and every fire that blazes at night a [true] fire?")
i.e. وَكُلِّ نَارٍ ("and every fire").

ukberi-tibyan:68-68.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَوْلَا كِتَابٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ سَبَقَ لَمَسَّكُمْ فِيمَا أَخَذْتُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ) (٦٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَوْلَا كِتَابٌ): كِتَابٌ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «سَبَقَ» is an adjective (ṣifa) to it. And (مِنَ اللَّهِ) may also be an adjective, or it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to سَبَقَ; and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "had overtaken you".

ukberi-tibyan:69-69.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَكُلُوا مِمَّا غَنِمْتُمْ حَلَالًا طَيِّبًا وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) (٦٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حَلَالًا طَيِّبًا): this has been mentioned in al-Baqara.

ukberi-tibyan:71-71.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنْ يُرِيدُوا خِيَانَتَكَ فَقَدْ خَانُوا اللَّهَ مِنْ قَبْلُ فَأَمْكَنَ مِنْهُمْ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ) (٧١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (خِيَانَتَكَ): the maṣdar (verbal noun) of خَانَ يَخُونُ. The origin of the yāʾ is wāw; it was changed because what precedes it has kasra and the alif comes after it.

ukberi-tibyan:72-72.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَهَاجَرُوا وَجَاهَدُوا بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَالَّذِينَ آوَوْا وَنَصَرُوا أُولَئِكَ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَاءُ بَعْضٍ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَلَمْ يُهَاجِرُوا مَا لَكُمْ مِنْ وَلَايَتِهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ حَتَّى يُهَاجِرُوا وَإِنِ اسْتَنْصَرُوكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ فَعَلَيْكُمُ النَّصْرُ إِلَّا عَلَى قَوْمٍ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ مِيثَاقٌ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ) (٧٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ وَلَايَتِهِمْ): it is read with fatḥa on the wāw and with kasra, and they are two dialectal forms. It is also said: with kasra it means "authority" (al-imāra), and with fatḥa it is from mutual alliance in support.

ukberi-tibyan:73-73.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَاءُ بَعْضٍ إِلَّا تَفْعَلُوهُ تَكُنْ فِتْنَةٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَفَسَادٌ كَبِيرٌ) (٧٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا تَفْعَلُوهُ): the hāʾ refers to the support (al-naṣr). It is also said: to the alliance and mutual consultation.

ukberi-tibyan:75-75.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْ بَعْدُ وَهَاجَرُوا وَجَاهَدُوا مَعَكُمْ فَأُولَئِكَ مِنْكُمْ وَأُولُو الْأَرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَى بِبَعْضٍ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ) (٧٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ): in the position of the accusative by (أَوْلَى), i.e. "that is established in the Book of Allah".
